title: Go forth (Genesis 12:1–9)
hookLine: Abram, seventy-five, leaves his country for a land God will show him
carry: go, and I will show you

lines: THE WHOLE WORLD, THEN ONE MAN.
cards: Seventy-five can be an age for settling in: the house paid off, or close, a pharmacist who knows your name.

Abram, at seventy-five, packs everything onto animals, says goodbye to the town where his father died, and heads out with no address. Not a place he's seen in photos. Just a direction, and a voice that said go.
After eleven chapters about the whole world, Genesis zooms in on one old man and his first step.

teach.b: First, the call. In the Douay-Rheims: "And the Lord said to Abram: Go forth out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and out of thy father's house, and come into the land which I shall shew thee."
Three circles to leave, each closer than the last: country, kindred, father's house. And in exchange, a land God hasn't named yet.

teach.h: THE MAP COMES AFTER THE STEP.
teach.b: The map comes after the step. In Hebrew, go forth is lekh lekha, and some Jewish teachers hear it as go to yourself, as if leaving home were also a way of becoming who you are. Second, the promise.
I will make of thee a great nation, God says, and make thy name great.
Notice the echo: at Babel, people tried to make a name for themselves; here, God gives one. Then the widest line: in thee shall all the families of the earth be blessed. Not just Abram's family.
Genesis doesn't record a word from Abram. He went, as the Lord had told him. He took Sarai, his nephew Lot, and everything they had, walked to Canaan, and built altars along the way.

teach.h: GO FORTH OUT OF THY COUNTRY.
teach.b: Fourth, how the Church remembers him. The Letter to the Hebrews says Abraham went out not knowing where he was going.
The Catechism calls him the father of all who believe, and at Mass, the first Eucharistic Prayer names him our father in faith.
The Catechism holds him up as a model of faith: not knowing the whole map, but taking the first step.

how: Catholics call Abraham their father in faith; he is named in the Roman Canon at Mass, and the call of Abram (Genesis 12:1–4) is read on the Second Sunday of Lent in one year of the cycle.

o: the command to fill and rule the earth
a blessing said when a pilgrim leaves home
God's call to Abram to leave for a new land

games.q: what's inside the call — tap the pairs.
p: go forth, or go to yourself

s: God shows Abram the land before he leaves
the land is one "which I shall shew thee." the map comes after the step.
Genesis records Abram's long answer to God
the text records no word from him. he just went.
the promise is that all the families of the earth will be blessed in Abram
not only his own family. everyone.

games.q: you're Abram, seventy-five. a voice tells you to leave your country, your kin and your father's house, for a land it hasn't named yet. what do you do?
o: ask to see the land first.
go, as the Lord told you.
games.why: Genesis gives no speech: Abram went, as the Lord had told him, with Sarai, Lot and everything they had.

practice: Think of something waiting on you to have it all figured out first: a conversation, a change, a call you keep not making.
Notice how much of the map you want before you'll move, then ask only for the first step, and picture taking it. If you pray, you can ask God to show the next part when it's time.

wordCard.voice: Go forth. Lekh lekha in Hebrew: God's call to Abram to leave his country for a land not yet shown. He went, at seventy-five.

orig.note: Hebrew: go forth, literally go for yourself. Jewish tradition names this part of Genesis by these words.

carryVoice: Your line: go, and I will show you. Abram didn't need the address first. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: And the Lord said to Abram: Go forth out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and out of thy father's house, and come into the land which I shall shew thee.
